subject: Post-call: Stakeholder map, procurement path & SLA targets
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ross <alex.ross@acmehealth.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Stakeholder map, procurement path & SLA targets

Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for your time on the demo today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so we all have the same expectations: 

1) Decision makers and roles (as we heard on the call)
   - Economic buyer: Priya Shah (VP Product) — owns budget and ROI questions
   - Security/legal: Security Review Team + Legal (Procurement is copied) — will drive SOC2, network/KMS questions
   - Platform/Infra owner: DevOps lead / Platform eng (you mentioned Miguel) — cares about deployment mode and latency SLA
   - End-user champions: Clinical Insights team (data scientists) — care about inference quality and cost-per-call

2) Key decision criteria we logged
   - Latency SLO: p95 < 500ms for 512-token requests (target)
   - Cost target: <$0.008 per 1k tokens (goal for pilot economics) — you'll validate against internal benchmarks
   - Deployment mode: Private VPC preferred for PHI data; evaluating Dedicated reserved capacity if latency is critical
   - SLA needs: 99.9% uptime for production; pilot can accept lower SLA with notice

3) Procurement & security path
   - Security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence -> you expect to route to Security by 3/20
   - Procurement requires standard MSA + SOW + customer-specific line items; Priya to intro procurement contact (copied)

4) Next steps (owners & dates)
   - I will send an initial SOW draft and a simple SLA matrix by EOD 3/15 (attached). (Karthik)
   - Priya to confirm the final list of procurement and legal contacts by 3/18. (Priya)
   - Security will request our SOC2/pen-test artifacts; Marissa will coordinate the responses. (Marissa)
   - Short technical workshop with Miguel and Platform team to validate deployment options and p95 numbers — propose week of 3/22. (Karthik / Rishi)

Attachments: SOW_draft_v1.pdf, redwood-sla-matrix.xlsx (see below).

If I've misstated anything above, please flag edits. Otherwise, once Priya confirms procurement contact, I'll loop in Legal for the SOW.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.com]

[Attachment: SOW_draft_v1.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: redwood-sla-matrix.xlsx (excel)]

Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@acmehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-16T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Stakeholder map, procurement path & SLA targets

Karthik —

Looks good and thanks for the fast turnaround. A couple clarifications from our side after syncing internally: 

- Latency: the clinical team will measure tail latency during their synthetic workload. If you can provide p50/p95/p99 for both Hosted and Dedicated (same model family) that would be ideal. 
- Cost: your target is fine for the pilot, but procurement will require a per-seat/per-request cost model in the SOW; we can work through that in the SOW iteration.
- Deployment: PHI must be kept in our VPC; Dedicated or Private are both possible — the deciding factor will be latency numbers + network egress behavior.

I'll confirm the platform lead (Miguel) name & email by tomorrow and loop him in. Procurement contact is procurement@acmehealth.com (copied).

One ask: Can Rishi or Marissa share the SOC2 report and the pen-test summary (redacted) so our Security team can start the intake? If you can attach to the HubSpot deal or send a secure link, that'd be helpful.

Best,
Alex
Head of Clinical Data Platforms
ACME Health

Subject: Re: Post-call: Stakeholder map, procurement path & SLA targets

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the quick reply and for engaging procurement. A few practical items from the Redwood engineering/ops side to help you prep for the platform workshop: 

- I'll prepare p50/p95/p99 latency numbers for the model variants we demoed (gpt-xx-small, gpt-xx-medium) for both Hosted (multi-tenant), Dedicated, and Private VPC deployment modes. Expect the doc by 3/19.
- For the SOC2/pen-test: we'll provide a redacted SOC2 summary and the most recent pentest executive summary via a secure link. Marissa will send the link and a short checklist of the typical items security asks for.
- SLA: our standard enterprise SLA is 99.9% with incident response SLAs and monthly uptime reports. For pilots we can offer a trial SLA at 99.5% with a rollback/fallback plan to Hosted in the event of sustained regressions. If you have a target MTTx requirement (eg MTTI or MTTD) please share and we'll map responsibilities.
- Procurement paperwork: We've prepared a canonical MSA + SOW template (attached); the only common negotiation items we've seen are data residency clauses, indemnity caps, and specific uptime/availability credits.

Please let us know the name of the platform lead and a few times you have next week for the technical workshop. We'll block 45 minutes to review deployment options and run a short load/latency estimation.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
